summary: The root TLL primarily refers to something that is old, worn out, or effaced, like ruins or traces of a dwelling.

headwords.def: أَطْلَلَ see 1, former half: and the same, latter half, in two places. اطلّ عَلَيْهِ He (a man, Msb) looked upon it, looked upon it from above, looked down upon it, got a view of it, or saw it; syn. أَشْرَفَ , (S, O, K,) [i. e.] أَشْرَفَ عَلَيْهِ , (Msb,) or أَوْفَى عليه ; (Ham p. 208;) properly أَوْفَى عَلَيْهِ بِطَلَلِهِ , i. e. بِشَخْصِهِ [meaning he looked upon it, &c., with his body; not in imagination]; (Er-Rághib, TA;) and signifies the same: (K:) and so أَطَفَّ عليه .
